notes:
Summary: Archimedes is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a latency-sensitive, safety-critical inference tier for in-vehicle assistance + offboard reranking. Primary driver is tenant isolation and predictable tail latency at peak. They run mixed workloads: short chat/assistant responses (<=128 tokens), mid-length telemetry reranking (<=512 tokens), and longer emb training-style embeddings batches. They are strongly cost-aware but will pay for guaranteed throughput if SLA covers tail latency and reserved GPU planning is clear. Key ask: traffic shaping primitives (priority lanes) that allow hard guarantees for safety-critical routes while offering best-effort lanes for non-critical batch work.

Quoted from CTO on 11/15: "We need hard p95 guarantees for the driver-assist path or we won't trust the system in production. Best-effort for analytics is fine, but the control plane must ensure isolation."

Important: they prefer VPC/private deployment, want KMS integration, and will require SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence. They specifically requested examples of per-route quota enforcement, noisy-neighbor mitigation strategies, and deterministic preemption policies.
requirements_summary: Workload: live inference (low-latency chat), reranking telemetry (mid-latency), bulk embeddings (throughput). Targets: sustained throughput 50k tokens/sec; peak bursts up to 200k tokens/sec for short windows; p95 latency target for driver-assist <= 80-120ms (512 tokens), p99 under stress < 400ms. Required behaviors: per-route quotas, priority lanes (safety-critical), tenant isolation (no cross-tenant QoS bleed), noisy-neighbor controls (throttling, preemption), admission control with backpressure, autoscale with reserved GPU pools, explicit fallbacks to smaller model variants. Cost sensitivity: will trade some cost for guaranteed SLOs but want predictable unit economics (token cost bands).
technical_assumptions: Assume Dedicated offering with reserved GPUs and pre-provisioned kernel profiles. Proposed capacity plan: initial reserve 8 x H100-class nodes (mixed with 16 x L40-equivalents for smaller models) to hit the sustained 50k tokens/sec target with room for burst. Prefer a configuration with two isolated GPU pools: (1) safety-lane pool pinned to specific GPUs with admission control and strict per-route token buckets; (2) opportunistic pool for batch/analytics with weighted fair queuing. Admission control to be implemented at the frontend proxy using priority tags, token-bucket/leaky-bucket shaping, and preemption policy that only evicts best-effort requests after warm-cold boundaries. Expect to validate with synthetic noisy-neighbor tests and real traffic replay.
poc_plan: Step 1: sandbox Dedicated environment (vpc) — provide infra access by 2024-12-06. Step 2: ingest sample traffic and run baseline: measure current p95/p99 for model m1-small and m1-large. Step 3: enable priority lanes and per-route quotas; run 48h stress test with synthetic noisy neighbors to validate isolation. Step 4: iterate on admission control thresholds and reservation sizing. Success metrics: p95 <= 120ms for safety lane under 95% of test windows; limited p99 deterioration; no more than 5% request failures for non-critical lanes. Expected POC duration: 4 weeks.
commercial_notes: Requested a dedicated pricing sketch for 12-month reserved capacity (initially commit to 12 GPUs, scale to 24 after Q2). Procurement wants separation of costs: reserved GPU base + burst pool chargeable by usage. Legal asked for a draft SLA that includes throughput guarantees, latency SLOs, and credits tied to missed p99/p95 SLOs. They also want a documented remediation and rollback playbook for on-prem deployments. SE has prepared a draft SLA (drive link).

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: ambiguous preemption behavior causing safety lane impact. Mitigation: explicit reservation pools + automated eviction policies + smoke tests before rollout. Risk: legal wants hard SLA credits that are costly. Mitigation: propose stepwise SLA with probation period. Risk: on-prem network constraints. Mitigation: early network proof-of-concept and runbook.
